concepts.title: The academy roles
concepts.summary: The academy director runs coaching, education and welfare, and plans each young player's pathway to the first team.

concepts.title: The analysis roles
concepts.summary: The head of performance analysis and first-team analysts: opposition reports, live feedback and post-match reviews.

concepts.title: The club leadership roles
concepts.summary: The sporting director owns the football strategy and the CEO runs the business; both answer to the owners and board.

concepts.title: The coaching roles
concepts.summary: Head coach, assistant coach and set-piece coach: who plans matches and training, and why England often says manager.

concepts.title: The data roles
concepts.summary: The head of data science, data engineers and recruitment analysts: who builds the club's models, pipelines and dashboards.

concepts.title: How the app works
concepts.summary: Short visual lessons in the order the concept map sets, with your progress kept on this computer and an export.

concepts.title: The performance roles
concepts.summary: The head of performance leads sports science, medicine and conditioning to keep players fit and available.

concepts.title: Your goals page
concepts.summary: Name your target role and write an if-then plan for when and where you study. Plans like this help people follow through.

concepts.title: The placement diagnostic
concepts.summary: A short quiz at the start marks what you already know so you can skip it. Even a wrong first guess helps you learn.

concepts.title: The recruitment roles
concepts.summary: The head of recruitment, chief scout and loan manager: who finds players, writes the reports and places the loans.

concepts.title: The Role Map
concepts.summary: The senior jobs in a club, who reports to whom, and the competencies each one needs, drawn as paths through this map.

concepts.title: The Lesson Loop
concepts.summary: Every lesson runs hook, see, touch, predict, do, lock in and connect: each idea is shown, touched, then practised.

concepts.title: Attacking and defending shapes
concepts.summary: Teams often attack in one shape and defend in another, like Man City's 3-2-4-1 with the ball and 4-4-2 without it.

concepts.title: Back-four formations
concepts.summary: 4-4-2, 4-3-3, 4-2-3-1 and 4-1-4-1: what each shape gives in the middle and out wide, and where it leaves space.

concepts.title: Back-three formations
concepts.summary: 3-5-2, 3-4-3 and 5-3-2: a back three with wing-backs for width, which drops into a back five without the ball.

concepts.title: Ball in and out
concepts.summary: The ball is out only when the whole ball has crossed a touchline or goal line, on the ground or in the air.

concepts.title: Cards and misconduct
concepts.summary: A reckless foul earns a yellow card, excessive force a red; two yellows send a player off and change the match.

concepts.title: Catenaccio and the sweeper
concepts.summary: A spare defender behind the line, from Rappan's verrou of the 1930s to Italy's catenaccio. Its inventor is contested.

concepts.title: First laws, first passes
concepts.summary: The FA wrote the first Laws in 1863, and passing and combination play soon replaced the lone dribble.

concepts.title: Formation notation
concepts.summary: A formation counts outfield players per line from the back, so 4-2-3-1 never includes the goalkeeper.

concepts.title: Formation versus structure
concepts.summary: The formation is the base label; the structure is how the team really stands in a moment, rotations included.

concepts.title: Fouls and free kicks
concepts.summary: Careless, reckless or excessive contact fouls give a direct free kick; some other offences give an indirect one.

concepts.title: Goal and corner kicks
concepts.summary: Ball over the goal line: a goal kick if the attackers touched it last, a corner if the defenders did.

concepts.title: Hungary and the 4-2-4
concepts.summary: Hungary won 6-3 at Wembley in 1953 with a deep-lying centre-forward; Brazil's 4-2-4 won the 1958 World Cup.

concepts.title: Kick-off and dropped ball
concepts.summary: Opponents stand 9.15 m away at kick-off; at a dropped ball other players stand at least 4 m away.

concepts.title: Offside offence
concepts.summary: A player in an offside position is penalised only when active: interfering with play or an opponent, or gaining an advantage.

concepts.title: Offside position
concepts.summary: Nearer the goal line than both the ball and the second-last opponent, in their half. Level is onside.

concepts.title: The penalty kick
concepts.summary: A direct free-kick foul by a defender inside their own penalty area gives a penalty from the mark, 11 m out.

concepts.title: Boxes and areas
concepts.summary: The 5.5 m goal area, the 16.5 m penalty area, the penalty arc and the technical area, and what each one changes.

concepts.title: Pitch dimensions
concepts.summary: Law 1 gives ranges (touchlines 90-120 m), not one size. PL Rule K.17 sets 105 x 68 m unless the stadium cannot fit it.

concepts.title: Pitch markings
concepts.summary: The lines, circles and arcs of Law 1. A line belongs to the area it bounds, so a ball on the line is still in.

concepts.title: Players and substitutions
concepts.summary: Eleven players a side, at least seven to play on, and up to five substitutes in three windows in official competitions.

concepts.title: Position versus role
concepts.summary: A position is where a player starts; a role is the job inside it, like an inverted full-back moving into midfield.

concepts.title: The positions
concepts.summary: Goalkeeper, defenders, midfielders and forwards: the pitch zone each player starts in and mainly works from.

concepts.title: Possession and gegenpressing
concepts.summary: Guardiola's possession and Klopp's gegenpress, from Barcelona and Dortmund to City's 100 points and Liverpool's 2019/20 title.

concepts.title: The Premier League era
concepts.summary: From 1992: the back-pass ban, Wenger's Arsenal and Mourinho's 2004/05 Chelsea, who conceded only 15 league goals.

concepts.title: From Pyramid to WM
concepts.summary: The 2-3-5 Pyramid ruled early on; after the 1925 offside change Chapman's Arsenal made the WM. Who invented it is contested.

concepts.title: The referee team
concepts.summary: Referee, assistant referees, fourth official and VAR. The others assist, but the referee's decisions on facts are final.

concepts.title: Scoring a goal
concepts.summary: A goal needs the whole ball over the goal line, between the posts and under the bar, with no offence before it.

concepts.title: Semi-automated offside
concepts.summary: Since April 2025 the PL uses cameras to suggest the kick point and draw offside lines; the VAR still checks the call.

concepts.title: Squad numbers
concepts.summary: The old 1 to 11 by position, and the fixed squad numbers the Premier League brought in for 1993/94.

concepts.title: The throw-in
concepts.summary: Opponents stand 2 m away, no goal can come straight from it, and from 2026/27 a slow throw-in gets a five-second count.

concepts.title: Total Football to Sacchi
concepts.summary: Ajax's 1970s Total Football pressed and swapped positions; Sacchi's Milan added a compact zonal 4-4-2 and a high line.

concepts.title: VAR basics
concepts.summary: VAR steps in only for a clear and obvious error in a few match-changing categories, such as goals, penalties and red cards.

concepts.title: The 18-zone grid
concepts.summary: Six bands up the pitch by three across give 18 numbered zones, a shared map for naming where things happen.

concepts.title: The five lanes
concepts.summary: Five lanes run the length of the pitch: two wide, two half-spaces and the centre. Teams try to keep each lane filled.

concepts.title: The four superiorities
concepts.summary: Beyond numbers: positional (better placed), qualitative (better player) and socio-affective (players who understand each other).

concepts.title: Half-spaces
concepts.summary: The lanes between the wing and the centre, where a receiver can see the goal and both sides of the pitch at once.

concepts.title: Between the lines
concepts.summary: One pass can bypass a whole defensive line, and a player who receives in the gap between two lines is hard to mark.

concepts.title: Numerical superiority
concepts.summary: More players than the opponent in one area, like a back three against two strikers in build-up: a 3 v 2 overload.

concepts.title: Thirds and zones
concepts.summary: Split the pitch into defensive, middle and attacking thirds, then smaller zones, to say exactly where play happens.

concepts.title: Width and depth
concepts.summary: Wide players stretch a defence across the pitch and runs in behind stretch it in depth, opening gaps in between.

concepts.title: Attacking transition
concepts.summary: The seconds after winning the ball, while the opponent is out of shape. Leicester's 2015/16 title was built on them.

concepts.title: Defensive transition
concepts.summary: The seconds after losing the ball: press at once to win it back, as Klopp's teams did, or drop back into shape.

concepts.title: The four phases
concepts.summary: Open play has four phases: in possession, out of possession and the two transitions. Name the phase before the shape.

concepts.title: How phases connect
concepts.summary: Shape in one phase sets up the next: where players stand with the ball decides how well they defend when it is lost.

concepts.title: In possession
concepts.summary: With the ball a team builds up, progresses and creates chances, often in a different shape from the one it defends in.

concepts.title: Out of possession
concepts.summary: Without the ball a team defends in a low, mid or high block, choosing where to press and where to wait.

concepts.title: The set-piece phase
concepts.summary: Corners, free kicks and throw-ins restart a stopped game, so clubs plan them as their own phase, with a specialist coach.

concepts.title: Answer on the pitch
concepts.summary: Answer by tapping the pitch panel, for example where the space is, instead of choosing from a list of words.

concepts.title: One-question clips
concepts.summary: Watch Gym Level 1: a short reconstruction or local clip, with one question asked before it plays.

concepts.title: Reading a reconstruction
concepts.summary: Clips are animated from open event or tracking data. Each names its dataset and league, so a non-PL clip never says PL.

concepts.title: Short sessions first
concepts.summary: Sessions stay short and end before attention drops. You choose when to watch longer; the evidence sets no fixed limit.

concepts.title: Story, then structure
concepts.summary: Watch first for the story of the match, then rewatch with pauses to study the tactics, with the commentary muted.

concepts.title: Watch in blocks
concepts.summary: Split a match into blocks with a different focus each. Quarter-hour blocks are a research habit, not an analyst rule.

concepts.title: Watch one phase
concepts.summary: Pick one phase, such as one team's build-up, and watch only that, one team at a time, to see its pattern.

concepts.title: Watch one player
concepts.summary: Follow one player for a spell, such as a full-back who steps into midfield, instead of following the ball.

concepts.title: Watch one unit
concepts.summary: Follow a group, such as the centre-backs right after a turnover, or the striker while the ball is on the far wing.

concepts.title: Build-up structures
concepts.summary: How a team lines up to play out from the back: 2-3, 3-2, 3-1 or a box, like Arsenal's 2-3-5 and City's 3-2-4-1.

concepts.title: Chance creation and finishing
concepts.summary: Turning territory into good shots: crosses, cut-backs and through balls, judged by the chance quality they produce.

concepts.title: Positional and relational play
concepts.summary: Two attacking models: hold set zones across the pitch, or let players move close to the ball and combine. The labels are contested.

concepts.title: Progression and overloads
concepts.summary: Moving the ball up the pitch: breaking lines, overloading one side to isolate the other, third-man runs and rotations.

concepts.title: Defending the box
concepts.summary: Protecting the penalty area: centre-back positioning, blocking crosses and covering the cut-back zone.

concepts.title: Defensive blocks
concepts.summary: Low, mid and high blocks: how high the line sits, how compact the team stays, and which spaces it gives away.

concepts.title: Pressing schemes
concepts.summary: Man-oriented, zonal and hybrid pressing: who each player presses, and how the team covers the space behind the press.

concepts.title: Pressing traps and triggers
concepts.summary: Cues that start a press, like a back pass or a heavy touch, and traps that steer the ball towards the touchline.

concepts.title: Counter-attacks
concepts.summary: Attacking fast into space after winning the ball, as Leicester did on their way to the 2015/16 title.

concepts.title: Counter-pressing
concepts.summary: Pressing straight after losing the ball to win it back high, the gegenpress of Klopp's Dortmund and Liverpool.

concepts.title: Rest defence
concepts.summary: The players a team keeps behind the ball while it attacks, placed to stop the counter before it starts.

concepts.title: The set-piece coach
concepts.summary: The specialist who designs, trains and analyses routines with the first-team staff, using video and data.

concepts.title: Set-piece marking systems
concepts.summary: Zonal, man-to-man and mixed marking at corners and free kicks, and the spaces each system leaves open.

concepts.title: Corners and free kicks
concepts.summary: Designing routines for corners, free kicks and long throws: blocks, decoys, delivery zones and second balls.

concepts.title: Attacking player roles
concepts.summary: Roles up front: the inside forward, the classic winger, the target striker and the false 9 who drops deep.

concepts.title: Defensive player roles
concepts.summary: Roles in the back line: sweeper keeper, ball-playing centre-back, inverted full-back and wing-back.

concepts.title: Midfield player roles
concepts.summary: Roles in midfield: the No 6, the box-to-box 8, the regista, the mezzala and the No 10 playmaker.

concepts.title: Role signatures in data
concepts.summary: Each role leaves a pattern of touches and actions in event data. Every chart names its dataset and league.

concepts.title: Coach education pathways
concepts.summary: The FA and UEFA licence ladder, from grassroots badges up to the UEFA Pro Licence, the highest coaching award.

concepts.title: The game model
concepts.summary: A club's principles for every phase of play. Analysts code matches and review them against it.

concepts.title: Session design and methods
concepts.summary: Whole-part-whole, constraints-led games, guided discovery and feedback styles: how a coach builds a training session.

concepts.title: Tactical periodization
concepts.summary: Planning the training week around the game model, so physical, tactical and mental work happen together.

concepts.title: Developing first-team players
concepts.summary: Individual development plans, retraining a player for a new position, and bringing academy players into the first team.

concepts.title: The head coach's job
concepts.summary: Head coach or manager: the staff they lead, and how they work with the sporting director and the board.

concepts.title: In-game management
concepts.summary: Reading the game live, changing shape, timing substitutions and the half-time talk, with analyst feedback from the stands.

concepts.title: Leadership, media and pressure
concepts.summary: Managing a squad of egos, building culture and trust, and handling the press, the board and a losing run.

concepts.title: The opponent game plan
concepts.summary: Turning the game model into a plan for one opponent, with a Plan B and C, and presenting it to the players.

concepts.title: The weekly microcycle
concepts.summary: The week from post-match review to the day before the next game, for one and two matches a week.

concepts.title: Congestion and rotation
concepts.summary: Two matches a week in a PL season with cups and Europe, and how clubs rotate the squad to keep players fresh.

concepts.title: Injury risk and return
concepts.summary: Lowering injury risk, rehabilitation and the return-to-play decision that medical, performance and coaching staff share.

concepts.title: Load and GPS monitoring
concepts.summary: Tracking training and match load with GPS and wellness data, and the arguments over what those numbers really show.

concepts.title: Physical demands by position
concepts.summary: How much each position runs and sprints, and why ball-in-play time falls as a match goes on.

concepts.title: The analysis cycle
concepts.summary: Pre-match, live, post-match and long-term analysis, and who receives each output and when.

concepts.title: Analysis tools
concepts.summary: What coding and video tools do, how clubs use tactical cameras, and which free tools you can practise with.

concepts.title: Live analysis
concepts.summary: Coding the match live, sending short messages to the bench and building the half-time clip package.

concepts.title: The opposition dossier
concepts.summary: Build-up, pressing, transitions, set pieces, key players and weak spots, turned into a plan the coach can use.

concepts.title: Post-match analysis
concepts.summary: Team and unit reviews, individual clips for players, and KPIs that combine data with video.

concepts.title: Running the analysis department
concepts.summary: Team structure, weekly deadlines, earning the coaches' trust and hiring analysts: the head of analysis job.

concepts.title: The match note
concepts.summary: Turn what you watched into three short lines: what happened, why it happened, and the evidence you saw.

concepts.title: Rubrics and model answers
concepts.summary: Each output is scored for clarity, evidence, structure and actionability, then compared with a model answer.

concepts.title: Report templates
concepts.summary: Tactical, opposition, post-match, scouting and board reports each get a template, and the scaffolding fades over time.

concepts.title: Spoken briefings
concepts.summary: The 60-second match summary, the three-point half-time talk and the coach or board presentation, recorded on this computer.

concepts.title: Clips, stills and annotations
concepts.summary: Pick the clip or still that proves the point, annotate the frame, and build a one-page report graphic.

concepts.title: Data quality traps
concepts.summary: Provider definitions that differ, fixed-size frames that bend real distances, and sources that vanish: check before you trust.

concepts.title: Event and tracking data
concepts.summary: Event data logs each on-ball action; tracking logs every player many times a second. Open PL tracking is almost absent.

concepts.title: Open data and licences
concepts.summary: StatsBomb, Wyscout, DFL, SkillCorner, Metrica: what each holds for the PL, and what its licence lets you share.

concepts.title: Coordinates and kloppy
concepts.summary: Providers draw the pitch differently (StatsBomb 120 x 80, Wyscout 0-100); kloppy converts them to one standard.

concepts.title: Expected goals (xG)
concepts.summary: The chance a shot becomes a goal, from where and how it was taken. Built here on open StatsBomb PL 2015/16 events.

concepts.title: Per 90 and possession
concepts.summary: Scale counts to 90 minutes and adjust defending for how much the ball the team had, so players compare fairly.

concepts.title: Pitch control
concepts.summary: Which team would reach each point of the pitch first. It needs tracking data, so lessons use labelled non-PL open tracking.

concepts.title: Possession value models
concepts.summary: xT, VAEP, OBV and EPV value every action by how much it raises the chance of scoring soon after.

concepts.title: KPIs by position
concepts.summary: The numbers that matter for each role, from a ball-playing centre-back to a pressing No 9, and good, elite and worrying values.

concepts.title: Misleading stats
concepts.summary: Tackles inflated by low possession, safe-pass completion, assists without xA, distance-covered myths and cherry-picked radars.

concepts.title: Stability and fair comparison
concepts.summary: Which stats repeat season to season, how many minutes you need, and comparing two players in the same role and context.

concepts.title: Shot maps and networks
concepts.summary: In-browser Python on open StatsBomb events: load a match, draw a shot map, a pass network and a radar.

concepts.title: Build xG and xT
concepts.summary: Fit a simple xG model and compute expected threat step by step, then compare your numbers with the published ones.

concepts.title: Tracking data in Python
concepts.summary: Load open DFL Bundesliga tracking with kloppy, labelled as Bundesliga, and compute pitch control frame by frame.

concepts.title: Models clubs use
concepts.summary: Player projection and ageing curves, league-strength translation, valuation, similarity search and match-outcome models.

concepts.title: Evaluating models honestly
concepts.summary: Validation, leakage, calibration and uncertainty, the risks of LLM-drafted reports, and whether a coach can use the model.

concepts.title: The ML toolkit
concepts.summary: Classification, regression and clustering taught with football: predicting a shot's xG, grouping players into roles.

concepts.title: Tracking AI and vision
concepts.summary: How broadcast tracking finds players and maps them to the pitch, and deep learning on tracking data, explained visually.

concepts.title: Building the data team
concepts.summary: Hiring data scientists, engineers and analysts, the team structure, and balancing research with weekly operations.

concepts.title: Data infrastructure
concepts.summary: Buying data, building the warehouse, pipelines and internal dashboards, and the build-versus-buy choice.

concepts.title: The research agenda
concepts.summary: Choosing problems that matter, quick wins versus long projects, and measuring what the data department adds.

concepts.title: Head of data science
concepts.summary: What the head of data science does, who they report to, and how the job differs at a giant, a mid-table and a selling club.

concepts.title: Stakeholders and adoption
concepts.summary: Turning models into decisions the coach, sporting director and recruiters trust, and presenting uncertainty plainly.

concepts.title: Grading and scouting reports
concepts.summary: Grade a player on a fixed scale and write a report a head of recruitment can act on, with footage behind each claim.

concepts.title: Live versus video scouting
concepts.summary: Live viewing shows off-ball work and attitude; video covers more players. Broadcast footage often misses off-ball play.

concepts.title: One player, ninety minutes
concepts.summary: Track one player for a whole match: decisions, body shape, scanning, off-ball work and reactions to mistakes.

concepts.title: The relative age effect
concepts.summary: In youth football, players born early in the selection year are often picked more, so scouts must allow for maturity.

concepts.title: The scout's eye
concepts.summary: What a scout looks for in one player by position and age: technique, tactics, physique and character, on and off the ball.

concepts.title: Data-led shortlists
concepts.summary: Narrowing the market with data: similarity search, league-strength adjustment and age curves. Whether data leads is contested.

concepts.title: Leading the recruitment department
concepts.summary: Running a scout network by market, scout KPIs and report quality, the budget, the window calendar and succession plans.

concepts.title: The recruitment workflow
concepts.summary: Data filter, video, live scouting, references and character, medical, then negotiation, and defending a target in the meeting.

concepts.title: Squad mapping and profiles
concepts.summary: Map the squad by position, age and contract, and write role profiles that match the club's playing style.

concepts.title: Contracts, wages and agents
concepts.summary: Wage structures, bonuses and clauses, renewals and expiry risk, and agents under the FIFA Football Agent Regulations.

concepts.title: How a transfer happens
concepts.summary: Target, approach, bid, negotiation, medical and registration, inside the transfer windows, and who does each step.

concepts.title: Player valuation
concepts.summary: Pricing a player from age, contract length, league and comparable deals, and the gap between asking and walk-away prices.

concepts.title: Amortisation and squad cost
concepts.summary: A fee is spread over the contract as amortisation; profit on sale beats book value; the PL caps squad cost against revenue.

concepts.title: Pathway, loans and sales
concepts.summary: From academy to first team through loans and the under-21s, homegrown rules, and why selling a graduate is near pure profit.

concepts.title: EPPP and academy structure
concepts.summary: Academy categories under the Elite Player Performance Plan and the foundation, youth and professional phases.

concepts.title: Long-term player development
concepts.summary: Maturation and relative age, individual development plans, the coaching curriculum by age, and education and welfare.

concepts.title: Club football philosophy
concepts.summary: The playing identity, player profile and coach profile that every football department follows.

concepts.title: Decisions and stakeholders
concepts.summary: Decision frameworks, biases like sunk cost and star power, pre-mortems, and explaining hard calls to owners and fans.

concepts.title: Hiring the head coach
concepts.summary: Profiling coaches with data and video, the shortlist and interviews, the contract, and when and how to make a change.

concepts.title: Multi-club ownership
concepts.summary: How club groups share players, data and staff, and the competition rules that limit it.

concepts.title: The multi-year squad plan
concepts.summary: A three-year squad map, succession for every position, renewals, the sell, keep or loan cycle and the window strategy.

concepts.title: The sporting director's job
concepts.summary: Sporting director, director of football or technical director: the remit, the reporting lines and how clubs differ.

concepts.title: Governance and club leadership
concepts.summary: The board, the owners' and directors' test, the football regulator, fan engagement, and balancing football with business.

concepts.title: Club revenue streams
concepts.summary: Broadcasting, commercial, matchday and player trading, plus sponsorship, fan engagement and how the PL shares TV money.

concepts.title: Reading club accounts
concepts.summary: Budgets, cash flow, debt and ownership models, read from a real club's annual report and accounts.

concepts.title: Premier League money
concepts.summary: Central broadcasting and commercial distribution, squad-cost rules, ownership models and the regulator, dated as of reading.

concepts.title: Premier League rules
concepts.summary: The Handbook's squad, homegrown, registration and pitch rules, read with the edition and rule number each time.

concepts.title: Saudi Pro League context
concepts.summary: Applying the PL lessons to the Saudi Pro League: structure, foreign-player rules and career paths, checked and dated.

concepts.title: The club leadership seats
concepts.summary: Then the sporting director, recruitment, academy and CEO seats, each ending with a portfolio piece you can show.

concepts.title: The football department seats
concepts.summary: In the Club Simulator you take the head coach, analysis and data seats: game plan, match day, dossier and a model.
